name: Cidade Velha, Historic Centre of Ribeira Grande
subtitle: A cultural property on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 2009.

parts.text: UNESCO describes the property in these words: “The town of Ribeira Grande, renamed Cidade Velha in the late 18th century, was the first European colonial outpost in the tropics. Located in the south of the island of Santiago, the town features some of the original street layout impressive remains including two churches, a royal fortress and Pillory Square with its ornate 16th century marble pillar.”
Cidade Velha was founded in 1462 by Portuguese traders. Wikipedia calls it the oldest settlement in Cape Verde and its former capital, and the first European colonial settlement in the tropics.
The Portuguese called it Ribeira Grande and changed the name to Cidade Velha, 'old city', in the late 18th century, after the capital moved to Praia.

It lies on the south coast of Santiago, at the mouth of the Ribeira Grande de Santiago river and 10 kilometres west of Praia. Part of the planned original layout is still there, including a royal fortress, two churches and a 16th-century town square.
